items.title: Eddie Bert interviewed by Monk Rowe, Danbury, Connecticut, November 20, 2001
items.q: So anyway Mingus got established in New York and he started this workshop. He and Teo Macero. And we used to rehearse quite a bit.

ctx.x: Good. Tell me about, if you would, the Charles Mingus Jazz Workshop.

Well I met Charles when I was with Benny Goodman the first time. We were in San Francisco and Clyde Lombardi, the bass player with Red, you know Red’s small band, well we were with Benny at the time. Yeah it was Benny’s band. Clyde was on Benny’s band. And he said, “there’s a bass player I want to hear down in the International Quarter.” I said, “okay, I’ll go with you.” So we went. They had four basses and drums. Right? And Mingus is playing lead bass. So that’s how I met him. And the next time I heard of him he…
Kind of piecemeal, or under different titles?
